title: Ordinal Credit Assignment: Multi-Step Reinforcement Learning from Comparisons Alone
abstract: arXiv:2605.06375v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Policy-gradient methods need a scalar reward, yet for many tasks no formula captures what we want, while judging which of two outcomes is better is easy. We study reinforcement learning that receives only such comparisons - no reward function, no reward model - in multi-step tasks. Groups of trajectories start from a shared state, and each action is credited by how its reward-to-go compares with those of other trajectories at the same time step. We show the expected update is policy gradient with reward-to-go replaced by its win rate against the population still running at that time, weighted by the chance an opponent is still running; in deterministic environments the update ranks actions by true value and the optimal policy is stable, whereas under stochastic outcomes it prefers actions that win more often rather than those with higher mean. translated_title: 序数信用分配：仅凭比较的多步强化学习
translated_abstract: 策略梯度方法需要一个标量奖励，然而对许多任务而言，没有任何公式能够刻画我们真正想要的目标，而判断两个结果中哪个更好却很容易。我们研究在多步任务中仅接收此类比较信号的强化学习——不需要奖励函数，也不需要奖励模型。多组轨迹从共享状态出发，每个动作的信用根据其未来累积奖励与同一时间步上其他轨迹的比较结果来分配。我们证明，期望更新等价于一种策略梯度，其中未来累积奖励被替换为该动作在当时仍在运行的轨迹群体中的胜率，并按对手仍在运行的概率进行加权；在确定性环境中，该更新按真实价值对动作排序，且最优策略是稳定的；而在随机结果下，它更偏好胜率更高的动作，而非均值更高的动作。平局附近的标签噪声或由位置偏差引起的噪声不会改变期望更新；只
tldr: 该论文提出一种在多步任务中仅依靠轨迹间两两比较（无需奖励函数或奖励模型）的序数信用分配方法，用动作在同一时间步群体中的胜率替代未来累积奖励，证明其期望更新等价于策略梯度，且在确定性环境中按真实价值排序、在随机环境中偏好高胜率动作，并对标签噪声和位置偏差具有鲁棒性。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes an ordinal credit assignment method for multi-step reinforcement learning that relies solely on trajectory comparisons—without any reward function or reward model—by replacing reward-to-go with each action's win rate against the population at the same time step, proving the expected update is equivalent to policy gradient, which ranks actions by true value in deterministic environments, prefers higher win-rate actions under stochastic outcomes, and remains robust to label noise and position bias.
